title: Cybersecurity Analyst Salary in 2026 (Real BLS Data)
dek: The U.S. median annual wage for information security analysts — the official category for cybersecurity analysts — was $124,910 in May 2024, with the top 10% earning more than $186,420.

seo.metaDescription: What cybersecurity analysts earn, from official U.S. BLS data — the $124,910 median, the full range by percentile, and what raises pay fastest.

sources.label: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — Information Security Analysts, Occupational Outlook Handbook (May 2024 wage data)
U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics

body.richText: Cybersecurity analyst pay is easier to pin down than many tech salaries, because there is a clean official category for it: the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics tracks "information security analysts," which is where most cybersecurity analyst roles are counted.

According to the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, using May 2024 wage data, information security analysts earned a median annual wage of $124,910. For context, the median wage for all workers was $49,500 — so this is a well-above-average field.

body.caption: BLS wage distribution for information security analysts, May 2024.

body.richText: The gap between the bottom and top of this range — roughly $70,000 to $186,000+ — is mostly driven by experience, specialization, industry, and location. Where you sit in it is more within your control than the median suggests.

Beyond pay, the demand signal is striking. The BLS projects employment of information security analysts to grow 29% from 2024 to 2034 — much faster than the average for all occupations — with about 16,000 openings projected each year on average over the decade. That combination of high pay and fast growth is rare.

body.text: What moves your salary within the range

items: Experience — the single largest factor; pay climbs steeply after the first few years
Specialization — cloud security, incident response, and application security command premiums
Certifications that match seniority — entry-level Security+ early, advanced credentials later
Industry — finance and technology tend to pay more than the average sector
Clearances — U.S. security clearances can meaningfully raise pay for government-adjacent work

body.richText: Entry-level pay is usually well below the median. A first SOC or junior analyst role often sits in the lower band, then rises quickly. Judge the career by the trajectory, not the starting number.

items.question: What is the average cybersecurity analyst salary in the US?
items.answerRichText: The BLS median annual wage for information security analysts — the official category — was $124,910 in May 2024. The middle of the range is a better guide than any single "average," and the linked BLS page shows the current figure.

items.question: Do entry-level cybersecurity analysts earn that much?
items.answerRichText: Usually no. Entry-level roles typically start in the lower part of the range, below the median, and pay rises quickly with experience and specialization over the first several years.

items.question: Which certification raises cybersecurity pay the most?
